question: What is the target time frame for delivering a baby via a Category 1 emergency Caesarean section?
explanation: Category 1 caesareans are done for immediate threats to life, needing surgical delivery within thirty minutes to protect the mother and baby. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why do midwives need to accurately classify the urgency of an emergency Caesarean section?

options.A: It helps prioritize theatre workflow and mobilization of the emergency team
options.B: It dictates whether general anesthesia must be avoided entirely
options.C: It removes the need to obtain formal written consent from the patient
options.D: It determines the exact type of skin incision the surgeon will use

explanation: Knowing the category lets the surgical and nursing teams prepare the operating room and patient with the right level of urgency. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h1)

question: What size of intravenous cannula is usually secured during emergency pre-operative prep?
explanation: A large-bore intravenous cannula allows for rapid fluid replacement and blood transfusion if heavy bleeding happens during surgery. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h2)

question: A frightened laboring woman needs an emergency Caesarean section but refuses to sign the consent form out of panic. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Ask a relative to sign the form without informing the patient
options.B: Cancel the procedure and allow her to attempt a spontaneous vaginal birth
options.C: Provide calm reassurance and briefly explain the life-saving reason for the surgery
options.D: Proceed with the surgery immediately without any form of consent

explanation: Calm communication helps ease panic, allowing the patient to understand the emergency and give informed consent. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why is a catheter used to empty the urinary bladder right before an emergency Caesarean section?

options.A: To stimulate regular uterine contractions during the surgery
options.B: To measure the exact volume of amniotic fluid produced
options.C: To eliminate the need for any post-operative urine monitoring
options.D: To prevent accidental surgical injury to the bladder

explanation: An empty bladder moves away from the lower uterine segment, lowering the chance of it being accidentally cut during the surgery. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which of these items is usually NOT removed from a patient before she goes into the operating theatre for a Caesarean section?
explanation: Essential items like spectacles or hearing aids are kept with the patient until anesthesia so she can communicate clearly, while jewelry and dentures are removed for safety. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the midwife's main responsibility right after the baby is born during an emergency Caesarean section?

options.A: Immediately transfer the baby to the neonatal intensive care unit
options.B: Complete the surgical instrument count with the scrub nurse
options.C: Administer intravenous oxytocin directly to the newborn infant
options.D: Receive, dry, assess, and provide initial resuscitation for the newborn

explanation: The midwife cares for the newborn immediately, making sure the airway is clear and the baby is warm and breathing well. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why is keeping a newborn warm right after a Caesarean birth so important?

options.A: It replaces the need for routine vitamin K prophylaxis administration
options.B: It directly prevents the development of neonatal jaundice
options.C: It prevents rapid heat loss and dangerous cold stress in the neonate
options.D: It ensures the baby passes meconium within the first hour of life

explanation: Newborns lose heat fast through evaporation; drying and warming them prevents hypothermia and other health issues. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h4)

question: How often should a mother's vital signs be checked during the first hour after a Caesarean section?

options.B: Once at the end of the hour

explanation: Checking vital signs every fifteen minutes in the first hour helps the midwife catch early signs of bleeding or anesthesia issues. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h5)

question: What does a soft, boggy uterine fundus mean when found during post-operative recovery?

options.A: It suggests that the surgical wound has become infected
options.B: It shows that the indwelling urinary catheter needs immediate removal
options.C: It indicates poor uterine contraction and a high risk of postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: It is a normal physiological finding after regional spinal anesthesia

explanation: A firm fundus squeezes blood vessels shut, but a soft fundus means the muscle is relaxed and bleeding might happen. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h5)

question: When is the indwelling urinary catheter usually taken out after an uncomplicated Caesarean section?

options.A: Immediately upon arrival in the recovery room
options.B: Only after the skin stitches are removed
options.C: After exactly 7 days in the ward

explanation: Removing the catheter within twenty-four hours lowers the risk of urinary tract infection and helps the patient start moving and passing urine on her own. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why is good pain relief a clinical priority after a Caesarean section, beyond just making the mother comfortable?

options.A: It enables the mother to cough, breathe deeply, and move around early
options.B: It stimulates immediate breast milk production in the mammary glands
options.C: It speeds up the complete involution of the postpartum uterus
options.D: It directly prevents the formation of internal abdominal adhesions

explanation: Good pain relief removes the barrier of incisional pain, letting the patient move and do breathing exercises to prevent chest infections and clots. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the main medical benefit of encouraging early movement after a Caesarean section?

options.A: Rapid closure of the internal uterine surgical scar tissue
options.B: Prevention of venous thromboembolism and deep vein thrombosis
options.C: Prevention of postpartum emotional baby blues
options.D: Immediate restoration of normal pre-pregnancy hormone levels

explanation: Moving early improves blood flow in the legs, which stops dangerous blood clots from forming in the veins. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h7)

question: A postpartum mother recovering from an emergency Caesarean section complains of sudden left calf pain, swelling, and tenderness on her second day post-op. What should the midwife suspect?
explanation: Calf pain, swelling, and tenderness on one side are classic signs of deep vein thrombosis, which needs an urgent medical review. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h7)
